recipes.name: Heather's Cilantro, Black Bean, and Corn Salsa
ingredients_raw: 2 (15 ounce) cans black beans, drained and rinsed
1 (14.5 ounce) can Italian-style diced tomatoes, drained
1 red bell pepper, seeded and chopped
2 tablespoons olive oil, or to taste

steps.text: Stir black beans, yellow and white corn, tomatoes, cilantro, green onions, red onion, bell pepper, and garlic together in a large bowl.
Gently mix in lime juice and avocado.
Drizzle with olive oil to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Heather's Cilantro, Black Bean, and Corn Salsa
raw_recipe.description: This black bean and corn salsa is an easy dip to make with 2 types of corn, canned black beans, tomatoes, avocado, and lime for a colorful party snack.

video.description: See how to make a lively corn relish for chips or as a side.

review.reviewBody: This is a really good salsa. I made it this past weekend and it was delicious. Things I did differently were : I used Fresh tomatoes not canned. About 2 medium ones that I chopped and took the pulp out of. I also added 2 tablespoons of TACO seasoning mix. This gave it a nice flavor. You can also substitute with cumin if you'd like. I omitted the oil and the avocado. I added about 1/4 cup of chopped jalapeno in. I let it sit over night so the flavors could marinate really well. With the leftovers I made black bean quesadillas the next day adding cheddar cheese to the tortillas. Will make again !!

This recipe is similar to my original corn & black bean salsa, except I used fresh tomatoes. HOWEVER, I finally wisened up and found a short cut - fresh pico de gallo from the grocery store produce section, canned corn & black beans drained. The only things you have to cut are the avocado and slice the lime in half. Cuts prep time tremendiously!

Love this recipe. Minus the Avacado this is exactly how i make my own salsa at home. I usually use a tropical fruit (mango, pineapple or kiwi) in place of the Avacado, but will now try with Avacado. Saw another similar salsa on here where edamame is added. Yum Can never have enough salsa...i use it to top so many recipes. As a lacto-ovo vegetarian it is so easy

So I took this recipe, as I do with all my recipes I find online, and changed it just slightly.

So I don't like using canned things so I used fresh corn (2 ears) and fresh beans (1.5 cups, dry). I also used fresh garlic (your recipe didn't specify) and fresh tomatoes (two Roma and a handful of cherry). I added other seasonings to taste ( garlic salt, paprika, chili powered, pinch of cumin, and Tony's creole seasoning). 

I kept everything else the same. Since I cooked dry beans the recipe time was much longer however if you have the beans pre cooked the time is about the same. (An additional 2-3 hours if dry beans are pre cooked).

Great salsa! I have made it several times now. I have made some changes, tailored to my family's tastes. I don't mix the avocado in it and it keeps longer, just have sliced avocado on the side. I use Rotel original (instead of Italian tomatoes), double the lime juice OR add 1/4 cup vinegar, and add hot sauce. I dump everything in a 1 gallon jar, shake it well, and let it sit in the fridge until the next day. I then shake it and dip out what we will use with a slotted spoon--that helps with the additional liquid without compromising the taste. This makes it almost as easy to keep on hand as the store-bought.

Fantastic recipe, the only tweak I would make is that I would add a second can of tomatoes and wait to put the avocado on as the absolute last step. We mixed it all together and the avocado got pulverized, next time I may leave them on the side. This recipe goes PERFECT with burritos, definitely a favorite!
I made this and second go around I used salt and the olive oil on the niblet corn that I roasted first and also used roasted red peppers. Fresh lime juice and fresh cilantro is a must.
I love this! My husband adds a can of mild Rotel to his portion… I wonder if I can freeze part of it…

I substituted guacamole pico de gallo in place of avocado and used two cans of fire roasted diced tomatoes instead of one. Based on personal preference I left out the pepper. Since the guacamole made it so creamy I didn't need the oil and it was really easy to scoop with a chip. This is one of those great recipes where it is good on its own, but allows you to tweak as you like. It makes a very large amount which makes it great for parties.

Delicious!! I do use fresh corn when in season (3 ears) and only one can of beans. Subbed a can of original rotel for the tomatoes for a little kick, used 1 tbsp fajita seasoning and 1 tbsp cumin and about 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes. Left out cilantro (don’t like it) but used fresh parsley instead. Very yummy!!!

My family and I love this recipe! I have always made salsa, but when I saw this version, I could not resist. The only changes that I made were: I slightly heat the black beans and corn for a minute with the garlic. This gives it more texture when it comes to the blending process. I also used fresh tomatoes instead of canned, a small jalapeño pepper seeded for a little kick and a teaspoon of distilled vinegar. I omitted the avocado. I will definitely make it again! Great recipe! Thanks!!!
Fantastic base but needs seasoning. I added taco seasoning, salt and pepper, and tripled the avocado. Add a little seasoning...it's a 10!
This was very good, but needed extra flavor. I added more salt and on the advice of some reviewers, taco seasoning. That put it over the edge in flavor and it was delicious.

Too easy! I made this without having to go shopping everything was already in my kitchen. I didn't have any fresh cilantro or peppers so I used dried cilantro from my spice rack and even without the peppers (did I mention that I didn't want to go shopping?)the salsa still turned out great. Maybe took 10 minutes max to make.
Love love love ❤️ also....add jalapeño!!!!

I didn't have green onions and I used three avocados. For the tomatoes, I used a can of Rotel diced tomatoes with lime and cilantro which another poster suggested because I had it on hand. I did use a little salt. I felt that due to the sweetness of the corn and pepper, the tanginess of the lime, the freshness of the cilantro, and the flavor of the onion and garlic, it didn't need any other seasonings. It was delicious. Next time I might use another can of Rotel or use fresh tomatoes. It was a big hit!
Not my fav! Too much cilantro and I love cilantro.
I added lots of onion powder, garlic powder, a bit of chili powder, a bit of garlic salt. I felt that is was rather bland without more spices.
This is an excellent recipe! It has been my go to black bean salsa recipe for 13 years! I printed the update and was glad to see it still posted
Good recipe which I found easy to snack on for a few days
